_metadata.title: ComplianceLint Interim Standard for EU AI Act Article 9: Risk Management System
_metadata.disclaimer: This is an interim checklist developed by ComplianceLint. It is not a harmonised standard and does not itself give a presumption of conformity. A harmonised standard on risk management systems for AI systems is being developed by CEN and CENELEC under Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 3871, Annex I, point 1. No official date for publication of its reference in the Official Journal of the European Union has been announced.
basis: EU AI Act Recitals 65-67 (legislative intent on risk management)
ISO 14971:2019 — Medical device risk management (adapted for AI)
NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
_metadata.awaiting_standard: A harmonised standard on risk management systems for AI systems is being developed by CEN and CENELEC under Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 3871, Annex I, point 1. No official date for publication of its reference in the Official Journal of the European Union has been announced.

requirements.title: Risk Management System Documentation
requirements.requirement: The provider MUST establish, implement, document, and maintain a risk management system throughout the entire lifecycle of the high-risk AI system.
requirements.rationale: Art. 9(1) requires a risk management system to be established, implemented, documented and maintained; Art. 9(2) describes it as 'a continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of a high-risk AI system, requiring regular systematic review and updating'. A one-time assessment does not meet this. Under Art. 9(10), providers subject to requirements regarding internal risk management processes under other relevant provisions of Union law may make these aspects part of, or combine them with, those procedures.
acceptable_implementations: Dedicated risk_assessment.md or risk management plan document
Risk register (spreadsheet, database, or structured file) with identified risks
Formal FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) document
ISO 14971 or ISO/IEC 23894 compliant risk management file
Risk management section in system design documentation
not_acceptable: One-time risk assessment with no update mechanism
Risk management only in meeting notes or emails

requirements.title: Risk Identification and Analysis
requirements.requirement: The provider MUST identify and analyse the known and the reasonably foreseeable risks that the high-risk AI system can pose to health, safety or fundamental rights when used in accordance with its intended purpose (Article 9(2)(a)), and MUST estimate and evaluate the risks that may emerge when it is used in accordance with its intended purpose and under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse (Article 9(2)(b)). The risks concerned are only those which may be reasonably mitigated or eliminated through the development or design of the system, or the provision of adequate technical information (Article 9(3)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 9(2)(a) covers the identification and analysis of risks when the system is used in accordance with its intended purpose; Art. 9(2)(b) adds the estimation and evaluation of risks under the intended purpose and under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse. The risks concern health, safety and fundamental rights, not only technical failures.
required_content: List of identified risks (severity and likelihood ratings are a common method; the Regulation prescribes no rating scheme)
Analysis of risks from intended use scenarios
Analysis of risks from reasonably foreseeable misuse
Consideration of risks to health, safety, and fundamental rights
Optional: risk categorisation (e.g. technical, ethical, societal, legal); the Regulation does not require one
acceptable_implementations: Risk register with risk ID, description, category, likelihood, severity, and risk score
FMEA table with failure modes, effects, severity, occurrence, and detection ratings
Structured threat modeling document (STRIDE, LINDDUN for privacy)
NIST AI RMF MAP function outputs

requirements.title: Post-Market Risk Evaluation
requirements.requirement: The provider MUST evaluate other risks possibly arising, based on the analysis of data gathered from the post-market monitoring system referred to in Article 72 (Article 9(2)(c)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 9(2)(c) requires ongoing risk evaluation based on real-world usage data. Pre-deployment risk assessment alone is insufficient.
acceptable_implementations: Documented process for incorporating post-market monitoring findings into risk register
Incident tracking linked to risk assessment updates
Periodic risk review schedule tied to monitoring data
Feedback loop from deployment metrics to risk scores

requirements.title: Risk Management Measures
requirements.requirement: The provider MUST adopt appropriate and targeted risk management measures designed to address the identified risks (Article 9(2)(d)). The measures MUST be such that the relevant residual risk associated with each hazard, as well as the overall residual risk, is judged to be acceptable (Article 9(5), first subparagraph). In identifying them, the provider MUST ensure elimination or reduction of risks in as far as technically feasible through adequate design and development and, where appropriate, adequate mitigation and control measures for risks that cannot be eliminated (Article 9(5), second subparagraph, points (a) and (b)), giving due consideration to the technical knowledge, experience, education and training to be expected by the deployer and the presumable context of use (Article 9(5), third subparagraph). The measures MUST give due consideration to the effects and possible interaction resulting from the combined application of the requirements of Articles 8 to 15, with a view to minimising risks more effectively while achieving an appropriate balance in implementing the measures (Article 9(4)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 9(5), second subparagraph, lists what shall be ensured in identifying the most appropriate risk management measures: elimination or reduction through adequate design and development in as far as technically feasible; where appropriate, mitigation and control measures for risks that cannot be eliminated; and the provision of information under Art. 13 and, where appropriate, training to deployers. Art. 9(4) concerns the combined application of the requirements of Articles 8 to 15, not the combination of individual risks.
required_content: For each identified risk: the measure adopted with its rationale, and the judgement that the residual risk associated with each hazard and the overall residual risk are acceptable (Art. 9(5))
Evidence that elimination was considered before mitigation
Assessment of the effects and possible interaction resulting from the combined application of the requirements of Articles 8 to 15 (Art. 9(4))
Justification of the balance struck in implementing the measures (Art. 9(4))
acceptable_implementations: Risk treatment plan with risk ID linked to specific mitigations
Design controls document showing risk-driven design decisions
Code-level safety checks, guardrails, and input validation linked to risk items
Operational controls and monitoring procedures for residual risks

requirements.title: Testing with Appropriate Metrics and Thresholds
requirements.requirement: The high-risk AI system MUST be tested for the purpose of identifying the most appropriate and targeted risk management measures; testing MUST ensure that the system performs consistently for its intended purpose and complies with the requirements of Articles 8 to 15 (Article 9(6)). Testing MUST be performed, as appropriate, at any time throughout the development process and, in any event, prior to placing on the market or putting into service, against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose (Article 9(8)). Testing procedures MAY include testing in real-world conditions in accordance with Article 60 (Article 9(7)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 9(6) and 9(8) require that risk management is validated through testing, not only documented. Art. 9(8) requires testing 'against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system'; the Regulation names no specific metrics.
required_content: Test plans linked to identified risks
Metrics defined before testing (e.g. accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC; the Regulation names none)
Probabilistic thresholds defined before testing and appropriate to the intended purpose
Test results documenting whether thresholds were met
Evaluation against intended purpose and foreseeable conditions
acceptable_implementations: Automated test suites with documented coverage of risk scenarios
Benchmark evaluation scripts with threshold assertions
Model evaluation reports with metrics and pass/fail criteria
Red-teaming or adversarial testing results
Performance evaluation across demographic subgroups (fairness testing)
not_acceptable: Tests without prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds
Testing whose results are not recorded against the prior defined metrics and thresholds

requirements.title: Consideration of Persons under 18 and Other Vulnerable Groups
requirements.requirement: When implementing the risk management system, the provider MUST give consideration to whether, in view of its intended purpose, the high-risk AI system is likely to have an adverse impact on persons under the age of 18 and, as appropriate, other vulnerable groups (Article 9(9)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 9(9) requires providers to 'give consideration to whether in view of its intended purpose the high-risk AI system is likely to have an adverse impact on persons under the age of 18 and, as appropriate, other vulnerable groups'. The consideration is required for every high-risk AI system, not only for systems intended for children.
acceptable_implementations: Dedicated section in risk assessment for child-specific risks
Age-appropriate design assessment
Child safety impact analysis
Consultation with child development or protection experts
requirements.note: The consideration applies to every high-risk AI system. Where the provider concludes that no adverse impact on persons under 18 or other vulnerable groups is likely, it should document that conclusion and its reasons.

requirements.title: Information and Training for Deployers
requirements.requirement: In identifying the risk management measures, the provider MUST ensure the provision of the information required pursuant to Article 13 and, where appropriate, training to deployers (Article 9(5), second subparagraph, point (c)). This includes, in the instructions for use, any known or foreseeable circumstance which may lead to risks to health and safety or fundamental rights (Article 13(3)(b)(iii)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 9(5), second subparagraph, point (c), makes the information required under Art. 13 and, where appropriate, training to deployers part of the risk management measures, so that risks which cannot be eliminated are known to those who use the system.
acceptable_implementations: Residual risk section in user documentation or instructions for use
Known limitations document listing unmitigated risks
Model card with risk and limitation disclosures
Safety datasheet or risk communication document

scoring.compliant: R01 met + R02 met + R04 or R05 met + at least 3 others met
scoring.partial: R01 met + at least 2 of R02-R07 met
scoring.non_compliant: R01 not met, or fewer than 2 of R02-R07 met
